title: minibatch-phased-swap-with-session-affinity-and-rollback-oracle
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: Reduce user-facing variance during incremental model swaps while preserving session consistency and enabling automated, telemetry-driven rollback decisions. Existing staged-swap controllers either (a) split traffic at coarse grain and cause session tear, or (b) delay swaps until quiescence which increases exposure time. This change introduces a minibatch-phased-swap controller that performs: (1) short-lived minibatch drains with session-affinity mapping to preserve in-flight conversations, (2) a stateful bisection probe that quickly identifies a problematic cohort via progressive sampling, and (3) an external rollback-oracle that synthesizes model telemetry and prompt-based regression checks to trigger safe immediate rollbacks. Summary of changes: - New controller: controllers/minibatch_phased_swap.go implements phased minibatch handoffs and a state store for session affinity mapping and drain tokens. - Rollback oracle: services/rollback_oracle/ evaluates metric deltas (latency, exact-match regression, hallucination score) and emits deterministic rollback recommendations. - Telemetry hooks: instrumentation added to runtime request traces and per-session tags for cohort bucketing. - E2E smoke harness: test/rollout_simulator introduces deterministic replay scenarios and a small simulated traffic generator for canaries and A/B experiments. - CLI flag and CRD: addons/k8s/crds/minibatchswap.yaml and cli flags to configure minibatch size, max-drift thresholds, and oracle confidence thresholds. Why this is different: mixes short minibatch drains (low blast radius) with session-affinity remapping so ongoing KV-cache-heavy sessions remain consistent, plus a lightweight bisection probe that accelerates failure localization within minutes. Rollback decisions can be automated via the oracle or gated for manual approval. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for controller state transitions - [x] Integration tests with KV-cache warm/cold scenarios - [x] Canary simulation runs against historical traces - [x] Docs drafted in docs/rollouts/minibatch-swap.md - [x] Security review for session state store (RBAC limited) - [x] E2E run passed on staging CI (rerun after flaky test fix) Backwards compatibility: the controller is opt-in via new CRD; default behavior is off for existing clusters. Migration: no data migration required; sessions not pinned will fallback to default routing. Risk and mitigation: initial canaries run at 0.5% for 2 hours before increasing; rollback-oracle suggestions are logged and only executed automatically if confidence > 0.95 (configurable).

release_notes: Introduce an opt-in minibatch phased swap controller that preserves session affinity during incremental model swaps, plus a telemetry-driven rollback oracle. Configurable minibatch size, max-drift thresholds, and oracle confidence. Opt-in CRD; defaults disabled.
review_conversation: Ethan Liu: This looks promising. Can you explain how the session-affinity store scales? Maya: The store is sharded by ingress node and backed by an in-memory LRU with optional redis-backed persistence for very long sessions; the CRD controls retention TTL. Diego Fernández: We saw a flaky test failure in the first CI run — the simulator seed made a timing race. Can you add deterministic seeds? Maya: Fixed in commit d9f0ab3 and added retries for the timing-sensitive assertions. Priya Rao: Security ok, but add an RBAC note to docs. Maya: Added RBAC snippet and limited service account scope. Diego Fernández: Approved after test fixes. Priya Rao: Approved (security). Merge ready.
ci_summary: Initial pipeline failed due to simulator timing; rerun passed all e2e and unit suites. Lint and vet green. Load tests show <2% p99 latency regression at 1% canary traffic.
merge_summary: Squash-merged into main after approvals. Short release window scheduled; operator docs and quickstart added. Deployed to staging for a 0.5% canary followed by automated analysis from rollback-oracle.
notes_for_ops: Default CRD disabled. To enable: apply addons/k8s/crds/minibatchswap.yaml and set controller flags --minibatch-size and --oracle-confidence. Start with minibatch-size=64 and oracle-confidence=0.95. Monitor metrics: rollout.swap.success, rollout.swap.rollback_suggestions, sessions.affinity_misses.
post_deploy_observations: Staging run: first 2-hour 0.5% canary completed with no oracle-triggered rollbacks. The bisection probe isolated a transient cohort with higher hallucination_score and suggested rollback which was manually reviewed and then auto-applied on a subsequent failing run.
security_notes: Session-affinity store runs under limited SA; no plaintext PII stored. Oracle only receives aggregated metrics and hashed prompt fingerprints. RBAC manifests included and reviewed by security.
qa_steps: 1) Apply CRD and deploy controller in staging. 2) Start a small canary (0.5%), run simulator trace against historical traffic. 3) Verify session continuity for long-running conversations and KV cache reuse. 4) Force a regression signal in simulator and observe oracle suggestion and optional auto-rollback. 5) Review logs and metrics for rollback_suggestions and rollouts.swap.* metrics.
notes: This implementation is intentionally conservative: controller is opt-in, oracle auto-actions require high confidence by default, and operator visibility is emphasized with opt-out gates. Future follow-ups: adaptive minibatch sizing, multi-tenant isolation, and a web console visualization for bisection probes.
